question: Can a molecular signature identify a tissue reliably?

tiles.label: balanced accuracy of a 20-gene panel
tiles.sub: 19 tissues · 899 vials · 50 animals · 5 animal-grouped folds, the panel re-selected inside each

tiles.label: mapped adult organs named correctly in another lab's rats
tiles.sub: rat BodyMap, 21-week adults: 9 of 11 organs mapped, muscle and brain as super-classes; 68 samples, 8 animals; panel fit on all 50 MoTrPAC animals

tiles.label: coverage of the 90 % guarantee there
tiles.sub: sets calibrated on MoTrPAC animals, α = 0.10; the shortfall is empty sets

tiles.line: mean of 20 draws · 1.00 tissue per set
tiles.label: observed coverage in another lab after recalibrating on three of its animals
tiles.sub: sets calibrated on MoTrPAC animals cover 0.618 there [0.58, 0.67], the shortfall empty sets; 3 calibration animals (≈ 25 samples), 5 test animals, α = 0.10

tiles.label: of the tissue signal is batch, measured directly on MoTrPAC's bridging reference pools
tiles.sub: between-plate variance of gastrocnemius reference pool 99 over the variance separating the 19 tissues, all genes; 6 extraction plates, both sequencing sites; 1.6–5.3 % across all 6 pools
tiles.source: results/16_identifiability/bridge_variance.csv (gene_set all_genes, pool 80001, Σ V_batch / Σ V_tissue)

tiles_identifiability.label: tissue pairs whose contrast exists inside one processing batch (ovary and testes)
tiles_identifiability.sub: RNA-seq plate, library batch and flowcell; the one pair is also the sex contrast
